description: What version every schema in contracts/schemas/ is, what its content digest was when that version was published, and what changed at each version (FR-29, NFR-21).

breakingChanges.change: A mapping must now declare schemaVersion 1.1.0. Nothing in the contract stopped being accepted and nothing became required, but the version is pinned with const, so a document still declaring 1.0.0 is refused with a version mismatch rather than validated against the newer shape.

history.migration: Change schemaVersion from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0. Nothing else in an existing mapping needs to change. Optionally add toolListPointer, naming where a binding emitted for this runtime carries its explicit tool list; without it the NEG-D check refuses every binding emitted for this runtime, which is the fail-closed state and not an exemption.
history.rationale: Added toolListPointer so the binding layer can state where an emitted binding carries its tool list. NEG-D has to read that list out of a runtime-shaped document, and nothing under contracts/ may name a runtime's properties (FR-04). The alternative was for the checking code to search an arbitrary document for something list-shaped, which is the inference the call-site check already refused to make: a check that guesses its own subject cannot distinguish an absent list from one it failed to look for. Versioned as a minor change because the contract change is purely additive and optional. The mandatory version-string update is recorded as a breaking change anyway, because it is what a consumer's untouched document actually experiences, and a register claiming nothing breaks while the validator refuses their file would be the register lying about the validator.
